doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: The Baked Potato and its low pay
summary: Rowe recalls the low pay at the Baked Potato; Frichtel describes the funky fusion room started by Don Randi.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: We went to L.A., it was over 20 years ago, and we went to the Baked Potato, and the people that were playing there were incredible. And somehow I guess I learned that they were playing for like $30 apiece if that.

Absolutely. Absolutely. Yeah I played at the Baked Potato many times. It’s considered kind of a jazz fusion room, and it’s a place you don’t want to see in the daylight. It’s pretty funky in there. But it was an L.A. institution as far as, I mean you could go there and you could see all the top session guys, and it was started by one of the guys that was in The Wrecking Crew, Don Randi, it’s basically his club. But I saw a lot of great music out there, and played there a bunch of times over the years. But there was never much money involved. You know, that’s for sure.
